subject: Prompt-cache billing scenario and rate card request
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@shoply.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on prompt-cache billing for our prefix-heavy workload

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked great. Before we move forward with a pilot, finance needs a clear example of how prompt caching would be billed for us. We have two quick scenarios:

1) A single customer request where the first 300 tokens (prefix) are identical across many users and the dynamic tail is 20 tokens. If the runtime returns a cache hit for the prefix, do you charge for the 300 prefix tokens on subsequent hits? If not, is there any baseline per-request billing?

2) The same prefix is used across two different routes/apps in our account (same Shoply org but two services). Are cache hits shared across routes, or are they scoped to a route or model instance?

Can you provide a short worked example (token counts x price) and the baseline ratecard you’d use for an initial pilot? Finance also asked whether Redwood can apply a one-time onboarding credit if we identify a billing mismatch during evaluation.

Appreciate the details — copying Finance on this thread.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform, Shoply
[sent from mobile]
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@shoply.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-08T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on prompt-cache billing for our prefix-heavy workload

Hi Sarah — great to follow up. Short answers up front, then a worked example and next steps.

- Cache hits: For hits served from an active prefix cache, you are not billed for the model compute that would have generated those tokens. We still evaluate request routing and small per-request metadata costs that are accounted for in the baseline API unit, but those are typically <1% of token costs for prefix-heavy workloads.
- Scope: Prefix cache is scoped at the customer (Shoply) + model variant level by default. That means two routes under the same Shoply account that use the same model variant will see shared cache hits (no double charge) — unless you explicitly pin routes to separate isolation pools.

Worked example (illustrative):
- List price (hosted API): $0.0006 per input token, $0.0012 per output token (pilot ratecard attached).
- Scenario: first request generates 300-token prefix + 20-token tail = 320 generation tokens. Charge: 320 tokens x $0.0012 = $0.384.
- Subsequent request (cache hit on prefix): cached 300 tokens are not re-charged for generation; only the 20-token tail is generated: 20 x $0.0012 = $0.024. Baseline per-request metadata/route lookup fee is effectively included in our per-token rates for hosted customers but we track a small fixed monthly minimum for very high QPS low-token calls — we can show how that would look for Shoply in the attached ratecard.

We can provide a pilot rate that includes: (a) a 90-day onboarding credit applied to the first month if you identify any billing mismatch, and (b) a measurement window to validate cache hit rates before finalizing committed throughput. Ben is on-copy to confirm feasibility and the typical credit size for deals at your scale.

I’ve attached the draft ratecard and a sample mapping CSV so your engineering team can run tokenized traffic simulations. If helpful I can set a short call with Ben and Marissa to lock in a formal credit proposal.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification on prompt-cache billing for our prefix-heavy workload

Internal note / customer-facing wording suggestion:

Neha — thanks for the quick response. Confirming the key product points we can commit to for Shoply pilot:
- Cache semantic: prefix cache keys include customer org id + model variant + normalized prefix bytes. That design is why different routes in the same org will share hits by default. If Shoply needs cryptographic isolation between routes we can enable route-level isolation (this will create separate cache partitions and means hits will not be shared).
- Billing mechanics: bill only for generated tokens when a prefix is served from cache. We will surface an explicit line item on pilot invoices showing billed generation tokens vs cached-served requests so you can reconcile hit-rate savings.

Credit proposal (flexible):
- One-time onboarding credit: $10k applied against the first invoice if Shoply identifies a measurable mis-billing or cache mis-attribution during the 90-day pilot.
- Measurement period: 30 days of sample traffic followed by an annotated billing report and a joint review.

Marissa — can you confirm margins on the $0.0006/$0.0012 pilot numbers and whether we want to push a tiered discount (5% at $50k/mo committed, 12% at $150k/mo)? I’ll draft the short credit T&Cs.

—Ben
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@shoply.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Shoply Finance <finance@shoply.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on prompt-cache billing for our prefix-heavy workload

Thanks Neha and Ben — that is exactly the level of detail our finance/legal team needed. Two quick asks before we finalize the pilot:

1) Please send a one-page billing note we can include with procurement that specifies: cache scoping (customer+model), sample calculation (as above), and the $10k onboarding credit mechanics (how and when it is applied).
2) Can you attach a brief note from security/compliance indicating that cache partitions are logical (not multi-tenant physical) and that data from one Shoply route will not be accessible to another customer? Our legal is asking for wording we can include in the contract.

If those two items look good, I’ll route the pilot PO to procurement this week. Appreciate the help — copying finance.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Platform, Shoply
